cands.bio: Republican candidate for California's 45th Congressional District in 2026. Worked as a Torrance Police Department officer from 1999 to 2025. Served on the Cerritos City Council from 2020 to 2025, and on the executive board of the California Joint Powers Insurance Authority from 2021 to 2025.
cands.gaps: I could not find where Vo was born or raised, or when he came to California. I found no record of him taking a position on data centers or on development and growth limits. I found nothing on his stance toward homestead property taxes, gun laws, abortion, school vouchers or charters, or teacher pay. His campaign site is silent on these. He did not complete Ballotpedia's 2026 candidate survey. I found no specific actions from his time on the Cerritos City Council, such as votes or ordinances. The only source available was his Ballotpedia page, which quotes his campaign website, so his city council work and police career are not independently confirmed. The only endorsements listed there are online voter-guide recommendations, which I left out as not notable.

qual.background: Torrance Police Department officer from 1999 to 2025 and Cerritos City Council member from 2020 to 2025. He also served on the executive board of the California Joint Powers Insurance Authority from 2021 to 2025. His campaign site says he helped balance city budgets.

back-police-order.evidence: Says on his campaign site that he will always back law enforcement, fully fund training and equipment for officers and federal agents, and increase penalties for fentanyl trafficking.

workers-first.evidence: Says on his campaign site that he supports secure borders, faster asylum decisions, and better training and resources for border agents. He also says he wants to modernize legal immigration so employers can hire lawfully, and says 'we don't need more racial profiling.' The site does not mention H-1B.

land-for-floridians.evidence: Says on his campaign site that he supports banning the Vietnamese Communist government and its affiliates from acquiring, leasing or renting city property in Westminster, Garden Grove or anywhere in California.

cands.bio: Democratic U.S. representative for California's 45th District since January 2025. Born in Los Angeles County to Vietnamese refugee parents. Served eight years in the U.S. Army, then worked as a consumer and employment attorney. Co-owns a pharmacy in Anaheim. Sits on the Armed Services and Small Business committees.

controversies.text: Missed 1 of 676 U.S. House votes this Congress (0.1%), counted from the roll calls through 2026-09-16. Longest run of misses: 1, 2025-04-28 to 2025-04-28.

In May 2024 Tran told Punchbowl News that Michelle Steel "came to this country for economic gain," not as a refugee. In October her campaign mailed fliers linking him to Mao Zedong; he called them "dirty tricks." Sixteen Asian American nonprofits asked both Orange County parties to tone down rhetoric.

endorsements.text: California Federation of Labor Unions, AFL-CIO; California Teachers Association; Democratic Party of California (2026 cycle)
Equality California; Sierra Club Angeles Chapter; California Environmental Voters; Planned Parenthood of Orange and San Bernardino Counties' Community Action Fund (2026 cycle)
Los Angeles Times Editorial Board and Reproductive Freedom For All (2024 cycle)

cands.gaps: We found no documented positions or actions by Tran on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign purchases of homes and land, or growth and land conservation. We also found no stated pledge on refusing foreign-linked or big-donor contributions beyond a general statement supporting campaign finance reform. We found no documented stance on a H-1B visa program or state contracts. Details of bills he has sponsored were not available in the pages we read, and he did not complete Ballotpedia's 2026 candidate survey. The campaign website text is undated and several of its claims, such as having "taken on the NRA," are not backed by specific deeds in these pages. We found no foreign-government ties.

votes.what: Ended the 43-day federal shutdown: funds government through Jan. 30, 2026 and three full-year spending bills.

votes.bill: H.R. 5371 (2025) Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2026 (Sept. 19 House passage)
votes.what: House-passed stopgap funding bill to keep government open through Nov. 21, 2025; stalled in the Senate and a shutdown began Oct. 1.

votes.bill: H.R. 1 (2025) One Big Beautiful Bill Act (final passage)
votes.what: The 2025 reconciliation law: extends the 2017 tax cuts, adds new tax breaks, cuts Medicaid and food-assistance spending, and raises defense and border spending and the debt limit.

votes.what: Bars Homeland Security funds going to Confucius Institutes and entities tied to the Chinese government.
Requires documentary proof of U.S. citizenship to register to vote in federal elections.

votes.bill: H.R. 1968 (2025) Full-Year Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2025
votes.what: Funds the federal government through September 30, 2025 at roughly prior-year levels (March 2025 stopgap).

votes.bill: H.R. 152 (2025) Federal Disaster Assistance Coordination Act
votes.what: Streamlines coordination among federal agencies delivering disaster aid (hurricane/flood recovery).
Requires federal detention of undocumented immigrants charged with theft, burglary or assault of a police officer, and lets states sue over immigration enforcement.
